<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we explain a general procedure for producing the
sites we will be working with. Suppose we want to study sheaves
over schemes with respect to some topology <MATH_0001>. In order to
get a site, as in Sites, Definition <REF_0001>,
of schemes with that topology we have to do some work. Namely,
we cannot simply say ``consider all schemes with the Zariski topology''
since that would give a ``big'' category. Instead, in each section of
this chapter we will proceed as follows:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> We define a class <MATH_0002> of coverings of schemes
satisfying the axioms of Sites, Definition <REF_0002>.
It will always be the case that a Zariski open covering of
a scheme is a covering for <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0004> We single out a notion of standard
<MATH_0004>-covering within the category of affine schemes.
<STRUCT_0005> We define what is an ``absolute'' big <MATH_0005>-site <MATH_0006>.
These are the sites one gets by appropriately choosing a set of schemes
and a set of coverings.
<STRUCT_0006> For any object <MATH_0007> of <MATH_0008>
we define the big <MATH_0009>-site <MATH_0010> and for suitable
<MATH_0011> the small<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>The words big and
small here do not relate to bigness/smallness of the corresponding
categories.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001> <MATH_0012>-site <MATH_0013>.
<STRUCT_0007> In addition there is a site <MATH_0014> using the
notion of standard <MATH_0015>-covering of affines<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0002>In the case
of the ph topology we deviate very slightly from this approach, see
Definition <REF_0003> and the surrounding discussion.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0002>
whose category of sheaves
is equivalent to the category of sheaves on <MATH_0016>.
<STRUCT_0008>
The above is a little clumsy in that we do not end up with a canonical
choice for the big <MATH_0017>-site of a scheme, or even the small
<MATH_0018>-site of a scheme. If you are willing to ignore set theoretic
difficulties, then you can work with classes and end up with
canonical big and small sites...
